doc.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017

title: Getting hired by Lionel Hampton
summary: A Charleston trumpeter in Hampton's band brought him to a rehearsal, he played How High the Moon and was told to pack his bags.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Tell me about getting hooked up with Lionel Hampton.

Well now this was something, a left handed something. My friend, I had a friend, who’s a Charleston fellow, from Charleston, South Carolina. He was a trumpet player, a hell of a trumpet player. First chair trumpet player. And he was working in the band, in Lionel’s band, and he came to me one day, I was working at a club up in Harlem. He said, “Zeke” he said, “man, listen, this musician, he has an opening for a pianist. He needs a pianist.” He said, “Come on, man, come on down. I’ll come and pick you up tomorrow and we’ll go down to the rehearsal.” I said, “Oh man, I don’t want to be involved with Hamp.” I’d

heard so many things about Hamp you know. And I just, I don’t know, I just felt I wouldn’t fit in there. He said, “Man, listen, leave it up to me. Let me take — .” He said, “I’ll tell you what, I’ll be here to pick you up tomorrow at 2:30.” And boy he was right there at 2:00 he was at my door. He drove me down to the rehearsal, 48th Street I think it was, I forget, that rehearsal studio. But anyway I went in and he said, “Hey Gates,” everybody was Gates. He said, “Come on and play one with me.” And the tune he called was “How High the Moon.” Well it’s a good thing, you know, I had been playing with groups that played some tempos like that you know. And I went right on through it. And he looked around and he said, “All right listen, Gates, pack your bags we’re leaving in the morning.” And that’s how it started man.
He almost didn’t give you a chance to say no, right?
